question: In triangle \(ABC,\) \(D\) is the midpoint of \(AB;\) \(E\) is the midpoint of \(DB;\) and \(F\) is the midpoint of \(BC.\) If the area of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(96,\) then the area of \(\triangle AEF\) is
solution:
For triangles with the same height, the formula \(\text{area}=\frac12\cdot\text{base}\cdot\text{height}\) shows that their areas are proportional to their bases. Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of \(\triangle XYZ\).

Since \(D\) is the midpoint of \(AB\) and \(E\) is the midpoint of \(DB\),
\[
DB=\frac12 AB,\qquad EB=\frac14 AB.
\]
Consequently, \(AE=AB-EB=\frac34 AB\).

Triangles \(ABF\) and \(ABC\) have bases \(BF\) and \(BC\) on the same line and share the height from \(A\). Because \(F\) is the midpoint of \(BC\),
\[
[ABF]=\frac12[ABC]=48.
\]
Now triangles \(AEF\) and \(ABF\) share the height from \(F\) to line \(AB\). Their bases are \(AE\) and \(AB\), so
\[
[AEF]=\frac34[ABF]=\frac34\cdot48=36.
\]
The required area is \(36\), choice D.
